title: Launch slate entropy reduction and initiative choreography
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: Multiple runtime/console/api initiatives are scheduled with overlapping cut windows, leading to high coordination overhead, repeated last-minute capacity contention, and fractured stakeholder signal. Objective: Reduce schedule entropy across the release slate by introducing an initiative choreography model and an operational runway scorer that ranks launches by OKR alignment, capacity cost, and risk. Deliver a lightweight process + tooling pilot (calendar-as-code + runway scorer dashboard) to reduce collisions and provide deterministic cutover guidance.
acceptance_criteria: Operational runway scorer prototype deployed in internal console showing normalized scores for all Q2 initiatives
Pilot coverage for at least 6 initiatives across runtime, console, and API with documented score components
Weekly launch interlock process defined and adopted by three stakeholder teams (runtime, console, API)
Collision rate for scheduled cut windows reduced by >=40% in pilot month compared to baseline
Runbook and rollout decision tree published and linked from the launch calendar
milestones: 2026-03-15: Kickoff + data collection (historical collisions, capacity usage, OKR tags)
2026-03-22: Scoring rubric finalized (OKR weight, capacity delta, customer impact, risk multiplier)
2026-04-05: Calendar-as-code spec and proto schema committed to repo
2026-04-12: Internal console dashboard wireframe and mock implemented
2026-04-19: Pilot interlock meetings run for first release cohort
2026-04-30: Pilot retrospective and decision: adopt / iterate / roll back
risks: Scorer relies on incomplete OKR tagging in initiative metadata (data quality risk)
Teams may game scores if not aligned on weights (governance risk)
Calendar-as-code adoption requires minor CI changes; infra bandwidth constrained
Dashboard surface could expose sensitive scheduling data (access control concern)
notes: Design approach: surface only three signals to avoid overfitting: OKR alignment, incremental capacity cost, near-term customer impact
Decision rules: scores above threshold recommend dedicated capacity escrow; medium scores recommend canary-only windows; low scores recommended to be scheduled during wide windows
Operational guardrails: mandatory interlock sign-off for any launch scoring above threshold; automated backoffs for overlapping high-score launches
